findings.where: The last section, 'Hostelworld, for comparison', which is also the page's closing note
findings.fault: The page's final word on trust is a critique of a named competitor. It ends by suggesting that a hostel 'can look thin there' on Hostelworld. A page meant to show that Manta is neutral closes by arguing against a rival.
findings.who_objects: The founder, for two reasons. First, the positioning says the trust claim 'names no competitor' and must never compete on Hostelworld's ground. Second, the Hostelworld affiliate application (#78) is still waiting on Hostelworld's consent. Publishing a critique of Hostelworld's scoring while that request is open puts the partnership at risk. A sceptical backpacker would also read a dig at a rival as marketing, not as an impartial method.

findings.where: The lead paragraph's promise ('This page states it in full') against the 'Ranking method' body
findings.fault: The heading promises the full method, but the parts that matter stay vague. 'Pulled toward the area average' gives no weight, and 'a handful… a few dozen' gives no actual numbers. The page never says what counts as an 'area', and never says what 'our checks' are, even though passing them is what decides whether a review counts. Only the decay rate is given as a figure.
findings.who_objects: A hostel owner checking why a 9.6 from four reviews shows lower, and a careful traveller testing the 'we publish it, not proprietary' claim. Neither can reproduce a score. The page sets up a promise of full transparency and then visibly holds back.

findings.where: The 'Ranking method' section, where partner tiers are mentioned
findings.fault: The page never says how Manta makes money. It doesn't say that hostels pay for a partner tier, or that Manta may earn a commission when a visitor leaves through an OTA link. The first question a visitor has about a free ranking site ('so who pays you, and does that steer what I see?') is left to inference.
findings.who_objects: A backpacker deciding whether to trust the order of the list. 'No hostel can pay for a higher position' reads as an assertion until the page shows where the money does come from and why that money can't touch rank.

findings.where: Whole page: the 'We publish…' voice, with the only person shown being the footer email
findings.fault: No named person or company stands behind the method. 'We' speaks for what is a one-person operation, and the only trace of who answers for the ranking is the 'luc@' address in the footer.
findings.who_objects: A traveller or hostel owner who wants someone accountable for the promise that no hostel can pay for position. The first-visit-trust rules treat a 'we' standing in for one person as invented proof, and a method page is where accountability is looked for.

findings.where: Under the 'How we rank' heading (no date anywhere on the page)
findings.fault: The method page has no 'last updated' date or version, so a reader can't tell whether this is the method in force now. The Hostelworld citation is dated, but Manta's own method is not.
findings.who_objects: A hostel owner disputing a score, or a returning traveller, who needs to know the rules haven't changed since they last read them. Item 13 of the first-visit-trust rules (dates that show the site is current) applies.

findings.where: End of the page, after the last section and before the footer
findings.fault: Once the method has convinced the reader, the page offers no next step back to the rankings it just explained, such as the Bali destination list. The only route is the nav or footer.
findings.who_objects: A backpacker who opened 'How we rank' from a listing, mid-comparison, on a phone. They now have to scroll back to the top and open the menu to resume, at the moment the page has just earned their trust.
